title: Stabilize SSE seq-window sanitizer and mid-JSON rescue to preserve toolcall ordering
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Fixes race where mid-stream SSE chunking could break JSON toolcall boundaries; improves ordering guarantees for fn/tool calls and recovers partial JSON payloads instead of dropping fragments.
description:
Motivation: We observed production incidents where SSE chunk boundaries split structured JSON payloads and toolcall sentinel tokens, which occasionally led to dropped function calls or out-of-order tool events. This patch adds a lightweight seq-window sanitizer and a mid-JSON rescue path to improve deterministic reassembly and preserve fn/tool ordering for OpenAI-compat streaming clients.

Summary of changes: - Introduce seq-window sanitizer that tracks a small rolling window of event sequence ids and rejects/repairs out-of-order delimiters rather than emitting them directly. - Add escape-aware coalescing for fragments that contain partial JSON objects (heuristic: unbalanced braces/brackets or unterminated strings). Coalescer attempts a local reassembly for up to 256 bytes of lookahead before marking an event as partial. - Add a resilient toolcall handoff: when a function/tool sentinel is split across chunks we queue and reserialize the sentinel to preserve its original ordering relative to preceding text events. - Add unit and integration tests around fragmented fncall/structured-output cases and an e2e playback test against redwood-openai-compat SSE consumer. - Small refactors and telemetry: metrics for partial_json_rescues and seq_window_reorders, and an internal debug flag to emit a trace header when rescue logic is triggered.

Checklist:
- [x] Add sanitizer + coalescer implementation (runtime/streaming/sanitizer.rs).
- [x] Add toolcall reorder resolver and serializer (runtime/streaming/tool_handoff.cpp).
- [x] Add unit tests for escaped delimiters and partial JSON scenarios (tests/streaming/).
- [x] Add integration test against openai-compat shim (tests/e2e/openai_compat_stream_replay.py).
- [x] Update telemetry + add console dashboard note.

Why this is safe: The sanitizer is opt-in for now behind a runtime feature gate enabled for the OpenAI-compat route. Recovery attempts are conservative (max 256 bytes, no speculative concatenation across unrelated event headers). Fallback is still to emit the raw fragments if reassembly fails, keeping behavior observable. No protocol-breaking changes.

Review thread (high level excerpts):
- Evan Wallace (review): "Nice focused patch. Two asks: (1) add a small benchmark to ensure sanitizer path doesn't regress p99 latency under high QPS; (2) make the 256-byte tuning value configurable via a flag or config var."
- Priya (author): "Added a microbenchmark and made the coalescer window configurable via STREAM_COALESCE_MAX_BYTES (default 256). Benchmark shows <3% p99 regression on our local harness for 1k concurrent streams."
- Miguel Santos (review): "Edge-case: what if delimiters are corrupted by upstream proxy rewriting? Suggest logging the original raw bytes to debug traces only."
- Priya: "Added a debug-only trace header and limited raw-bytes logging to sample rate 1/1000 to keep noise low."
- Ruth Chang (approval): "Tests look thorough; telemetry gives us visibility. Approve after CI green."

- Backout: gate can be disabled instantly; code path defaults to no-op when disabled.
